articles.title: Critical Pre-Auth RCE in Orkes Conductor Workflow Platform Exploited in the Wild
articles.executive_summary: A critical pre-auth RCE vulnerability in Orkes Conductor is being actively exploited in the wild, allowing remote code execution. This vulnerability affects Orkes Conductor versions 3.21.21 to 3.30.2.
articles.technical_breakdown: The vulnerability is due to an unauthenticated remote code execution issue in Orkes Conductor, which can be exploited by sending a malicious request to the affected system. The issue is present in Orkes Conductor versions 3.21.21 to 3.30.2.
actionable_mitigations: Upgrade to Orkes Conductor version 3.30.2 or later
Apply the patch for CVE-2026-58138
articles.telegram_snippet: Critical RCE vulnerability in Orkes Conductor exploited in the wild, affecting versions 3.21.21 to 3.30.2. Upgrade to 3.30.2 or apply patch for CVE-2026-58138.

articles.title: OpenAI Staff Accounts Compromised via Chained Flaws
articles.executive_summary: Researchers used a chained exploit to take over OpenAI staff accounts, gaining access to internal code repositories. This was a security research exercise, not a malicious attack.
articles.technical_breakdown: The exploit chain began with a bug in OpenAI's public help forum software, which was then used to exploit a weakness in OpenAI's login system. This allowed the researchers to gain unauthorized access to staff accounts.
actionable_mitigations: Review and patch vulnerabilities in public-facing software
Implement additional security measures for login systems
Monitor for suspicious activity in internal code repositories
articles.telegram_snippet: Researchers used a chained exploit to take over OpenAI staff accounts, gaining access to internal code repositories in a security research exercise.

articles.title: North Korean WaterPlum hackers infected 30,000 devices worldwide
articles.executive_summary: North Korean WaterPlum hackers infected 30,000 devices worldwide. A joint law enforcement advisory warns that the North Korean hacking group WaterPlum compromised at least 30,000 devices worldwide from December 2025 through July 2026 and transferred more than $10.7 million in stolen cryptocurrency to North Korea.
articles.technical_breakdown: Analysis of incident reported by BleepingComputer. The threat involves attack vectors targeting standard services. Further technical telemetry is developing.
actionable_mitigations: Review firewall and perimeter access logs for anomalous traffic patterns.
Verify all endpoint detection (EDR) agents are updated with latest behavioral signatures.
Audit exposed external assets and apply vendor security patches immediately.
articles.telegram_snippet: 🚨 *HIGH Threat*: North Korean WaterPlum hackers infected 30,000 devices worldwide — Impacting systems. Immediate patching and log auditing recommended.

articles.title: ShinyHunters hacks Clop leak site, threatens to extort ransomware gang
articles.executive_summary: ShinyHunters breached the Clop ransomware operation's data leak site, stealing server data and private keys. This could allow ShinyHunters to extort the ransomware gang, potentially disrupting their operations.
articles.technical_breakdown: ShinyHunters allegedly breached the Tor site through unknown means, stealing server data and private keys for the onion service. This could allow them to impersonate the Clop ransomware gang and extort them.
actionable_mitigations: Review and update onion service security measures
Implement additional security controls for Tor sites
Monitor for suspicious activity related to the Clop ransomware gang
articles.telegram_snippet: ShinyHunters breached the Clop ransomware operation's data leak site, stealing server data and private keys. This could allow them to extort the ransomware gang, potentially disrupting their operations.

articles.title: Can You Prove a New CVE Is Exploitable Before Attackers Do?
articles.executive_summary: A new CVE drops, but the question remains whether it can be exploited in the environment. Mythos-class AI is compressing the time between disclosure and working exploitation, increasing the risk.
articles.technical_breakdown: The gap between CVE disclosure and working exploitation is decreasing due to AI-powered compression, making it challenging to validate risk on traditional security cycles.
actionable_mitigations: Validate risk on a more frequent cycle, such as daily or weekly, to stay ahead of potential exploitation.
Implement AI-powered vulnerability scanning to compress the time between disclosure and risk validation.
articles.telegram_snippet: New CVE drops, but can it be exploited in your environment? Mythos-class AI is compressing the time between disclosure and working exploitation, increasing the risk of attack.

articles.title: SolarWinds Patches ARM Hard-Coded Key Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated RCE
articles.executive_summary: SolarWinds has released security updates to address a high-severity flaw in Access Rights Manager (ARM) that could lead to an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability. The issue affects all versions of Access Rights Manager 2026.2 and prior.
articles.technical_breakdown: The vulnerability is caused by a hard-coded key flaw in ARM, which could be exploited by an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code. The issue affects all versions of Access Rights Manager 2026.2 and prior.
actionable_mitigations: Apply the latest security updates from SolarWinds to address the vulnerability
articles.telegram_snippet: SolarWinds has patched a high-severity flaw in Access Rights Manager (ARM) that could lead to unauthenticated RCE vulnerability. Apply the latest security updates to mitigate the risk.

articles.title: TigerByte Cyber Emerges From Stealth With $3 Million in Funding
articles.executive_summary: TigerByte Cyber has secured over $7 million in contracts with US government agencies, including the US Space Force, the US Navy, and DARPA. The company has emerged from stealth with $3 million in funding.
articles.technical_breakdown: TigerByte Cyber has secured contracts with US government agencies, leveraging its services to support their cybersecurity needs. The company's emergence from stealth with $3 million in funding indicates its growing presence in the market.
actionable_mitigations: Review and assess the security posture of third-party vendors and suppliers
articles.telegram_snippet: TigerByte Cyber emerges from stealth with $3 million in funding, securing $7 million in contracts with US government agencies.

articles.title: Viral AI actress' hotline face-scans every caller, watches their mood
articles.executive_summary: An AI-powered hotline service, Talking Tilly, collects facial data and monitors callers' moods, raising concerns about data privacy. The service will shut down on September 27, but the implications of the collected data remain unclear.
articles.technical_breakdown: The service uses facial recognition technology to verify callers' ages and monitor their emotions during calls. The fine print of the service's terms of service is unclear about what happens to the collected data after the service shuts down.
actionable_mitigations: Review the fine print of the service's terms of service
Consider alternative services that prioritize data privacy
Disable facial recognition and mood monitoring features if available
articles.telegram_snippet: Talking Tilly AI hotline collects facial data and monitors callers' moods, raising data privacy concerns. Service to shut down on September 27, but implications of collected data unclear.
